article.title: GNU Coreutils 9.12 Ships With Faster cut, uniq, and sort Plus a New uname Labeling Option
article.summary: GNU Coreutils 9.12 adds performance gains to cut, uniq, and sort, a new uname -A flag, and fixes for a factor buffer over-read and a parallel-deletion race.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

GNU Coreutils, the collection of core command-line utilities found on nearly every Linux and Unix-like system, has shipped version 9.12, according to the [project's official NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS), which dates the release "9.12 (2026-09-14) [stable]." [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/GNU-Coreutils-9.12) reported the release the same day, writing that "GNU Coreutils 9.12 arrived today featuring bug fixes, fresh command options, and performance enhancements for this fundamental collection of system utilities." The [GitHub release tag](https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils/releases/tag/v9.12) for v9.12 is signed by maintainer Pádraig Brady.

## What We Know

The release includes several performance improvements to widely used utilities. According to the [coreutils NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS), "'cut -w' operates more efficiently when extracting the start of a line in multi-byte locales, giving 4x more throughput with typical input," while "'uniq -c' now operates up to 2.5x times faster on systems with unlocked stdio functions." The `sort` command also changes: "'sort' will now better use available memory and parallel operation when reading from unknown sized inputs like pipes," per the [NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS).

The update fixes a race condition affecting several commands that traverse directory trees recursively. The [NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS) states that "'chcon', 'chgrp', 'chmod', 'chown', 'du', 'ls' which traverse hierarchies with -R, no longer fail merely because files may be being removed in parallel." [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/GNU-Coreutils-9.12) described the underlying problem as one where "these utilities would encounter failures when using the recursive '-R' option if files were deleted concurrently during directory traversal operations."

Two security-adjacent fixes are also included. The `factor` utility "avoids a buffer over-read (CWE-126) for certain values," a bug the NEWS file notes was "introduced in coreutils-9.8," according to the [official changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS). Separately, `cut -d` "with multiple multi-byte delimiter options specified will correctly match the last delimiter specified," fixing a bug "introduced with multi-byte support in coreutils-9.11," per the [same source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS).

The `uname` command gains a new option: "uname adds the -A,--all-labeled option to label all output, one item per line," according to the [NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS). [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/GNU-Coreutils-9.12) described the new flags as displaying "labeled output with individual items appearing on separate lines."

File-copying behavior also changes: "'cp', 'install', and 'mv' now fall back to a standard copy if a --reflink=auto clone fails due to EDQUOT, ENOMEM, or ENOSPC," the [NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS) states, and separately, "'mv' now warns when copying extended attributes fails with ENOTSUP, e.g., when moving files to a file system that does not support them." The `env` and `printenv` commands pick up a quoting change, now honoring "the QUOTING_STYLE environment variable, defaulting to shell-escape style," and `env` gains a new flag, `--env0-from=FILE`, to "read NUL-delimited environment entries from a file," with entries "preserved exactly" when combined with `-i`, according to the [NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS). The `stat` and `tail` commands also gain awareness of two additional file-system types: the NEWS file states that "'stat' and 'tail' now know about the \"failfs\" and \"nullfs\" file system types," adding that "stat -f -c%T now reports the file system type, and tail -f uses inotify for these file systems."

## What We Don't Know

Neither the coreutils NEWS file nor the GitHub release page specifies a rollout timeline for when 9.12 will reach individual Linux distributions' package repositories, since distributions typically package new coreutils releases on their own schedules.

## Analysis

Coreutils changes rarely make headlines on their own, but the utilities in this package — `cp`, `mv`, `cut`, `sort`, `uniq`, `stat`, `tail`, `factor`, and the rest — run constantly in scripts, build pipelines, and interactive shells across effectively every Linux and Unix-like system. A throughput gain in `cut -w` or `uniq -c`, or a fix to a race condition in recursive directory traversal used by tools like `chmod -R`, compounds across the huge number of times these commands execute daily in CI jobs and automation scripts, even though no single invocation is individually newsworthy.
